rubric_items.reason: All eight design components CO-1 to CO-8 have at least one threat; the components that handle personal data (CO-1, CO-2, CO-5, CO-6) each have an information disclosure or identity threat.

Most threats are specific to the component (SQL input, unscoped count, count(*) as text, reuse of get by POST/PATCH). T-8 and T-12 are functional regression risks labelled tampering, not attacker threats.
Every threat has a mitigation that is cited or named as a new control for implement. T-3 calls the patient_id filter existing while T-2 calls it new, and T-5 leans on an uncited, imprecise statement.
The MVP no-sign-in gap is stated openly in T-6 and T-10, but the risk acceptance is asserted without a cited decision while assumed and questions are empty.
Clear and consistent; front matter and body agree. Threats are ordered by component, not by risk, and carry no risk ranking.
